draft.text: You came in to check on your progress after shunt surgery for hydrocephalus.
You are walking better and can go to the dining room without help, though you still need some support sometimes.
Your thinking has improved, and you can have conversations without getting lost.
You haven't had any new symptoms like headaches, dizziness, or balance problems.
Your memory test scores have gone up, and your balance and gait scores are better than before.
You feel more stable when walking but need to be careful when turning or on uneven ground.
Your coordination is slower, especially with the finger-to-nose test, but it's not too bad.
You don't have weakness, numbness, or changes in vision or speech.
Your daughter says you're better at having normal conversations now.
You're feeling more emotionally stable and less confused.
The next steps will be discussed at your next visit.
